key_insight: Adding Tikhonov regularization to PINNs resolves the non-uniqueness of terminal-state distributed optimal control for parabolic PDEs by steering the solution toward the minimum-energy control.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a numerically stable way to compute smooth, physically meaningful controls for PDE-constrained systems where many inputs can reach the same target state.
method: Embed the parabolic PDE, terminal tracking objective, and Tikhonov penalty directly into the PINN loss.
Train the neural network to approximate both state and distributed control while minimizing residuals and control energy.
Use consistency and error bounds to relate training residuals and regularization strength to solution quality.
evidence_signal: Experiments on the heat equation and Burgers' equation show accurate terminal-state tracking with lower-energy, smoother controls than unregularized PINN baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on residual accuracy, quadrature approximation, and the choice of regularization parameter, which may need careful tuning in practice.
paper_title: Tikhonov-Regularized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Terminal-State Distributed Optimal Control of Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
